solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What could make cow stand and low?

indicators.note: asks what the letters of the two words could be turned into, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle about getting a cow to stand up and moo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like the cow's moo, but it is the definition in its sense of dejected; COWSTAND is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low and feeling downcast are both synonyms for being in poor spirits.

clue.text: Daughter meets uncouth Aussie, a man with loads

parts.note: an ocker is a boorish Australian in Australian slang

explanation.surface: A daughter meets a rough Australian, a man who carries heavy burdens.
explanation.definitionFit: A dock worker loads and unloads cargo from ships.

clue.text: Humorous person gathering band at uni to make merry

indicators.note: gathering means the first piece gathers the band inside it

parts.note: a wit is a humorous person
a hoop is a band, as around a barrel
to be up is to be in residence at university

explanation.surface: A comedian assembles a band at college to have a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To whoop it up is an idiom for celebrating loudly and having fun.

clue.text: Loose low-necked raglan — it did for woman in garden!

definitions.text: it did for woman in garden!

indicators.note: loose means the letters are let free to rearrange themselves

explanation.surface: A revealing, loose-fitting top was the downfall of a woman in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman is Eve in Eden, undone by the knowledge of good and evil; a raglan is a garment with sleeves running to the collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual awareness is the playful reading of what Eve gained after eating the forbidden fruit.

clue.text: Old people at home in Lincoln hugged by two sons

indicators.note: hugged by means the two sons wrap around the rest

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, so two sons give two of them

indicators.note: in means the home piece goes inside the Lincoln piece

parts.note: Abe was Abraham Lincoln's familiar name
at home means in

explanation.surface: Elderly folk stay home in Lincoln, embraced by two sons.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested containers: 'in' acts first, then 'hugged by' wraps both sons around the result. Old people here means an ancient nation, not pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabines were an ancient Italian people, famed for the rape of the Sabine women.

clue.text: One wicked knight capturing a city

indicators.note: capturing means the letters before it take the next piece prisoner inside them

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
wicked means bad
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A villainous knight seizes a city in some medieval tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts A between the D and N of ABADN.
explanation.definitionFit: Abadan is an oil-refining port city in south-western Iran.

clue.text: It means starting again — here in the north-west?

definitions.text: It means starting again — here in the north-west?

parts.words: It means starting again — here in the north-west?
parts.note: the phrase means having to begin afresh, and in a crossword grid the first numbered square lies in the top-left, north-western corner

explanation.surface: A phrase for starting over, located somewhere in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: The north-west looks like a region of Britain, but it is the top-left corner of this grid, where square 1 sits.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes returning to the very beginning after a setback.

clue.text: Time is being limited for lady proposed to

indicators.note: the time word sets the limits on each side for the next piece

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A woman receiving a marriage proposal has little time.
explanation.walkthrough: In the song Daisy Bell, the singer begs Daisy to give him her answer to his proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: The old music-hall song Daisy Bell is a proposal of marriage on a bicycle built for two.

clue.text: Womenswear near menswear?

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near
ties are worn by men

explanation.surface: A shop question about whether ladies' clothes sit beside the men's section.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightdresses are loose garments that women and girls wear to bed.

clue.text: Muck churned over repeatedly — a possible feature of war

indicators.note: repeatedly means the piece is written twice
churned over means the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: muck means mud

explanation.surface: Mud churned again and again, a possible feature of a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churned over' turns MUD into DUM, and 'repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumdum is an expanding bullet, of the kind banned in warfare.

clue.text: Church with old Irish singing group

explanation.surface: A church that has an old Irish choral ensemble.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of singers performing together, especially in church, is the sense here.

clue.text: Usher round a French companion, eating late morning?

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the others, enclosing them

parts.note: to usher someone in is to bring them
UN is French for a
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: An usher turns towards a French companion and eats a mid-morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts UNCH inside BRING; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a combined breakfast and lunch late in the morning is the activity described.

clue.text: No longer wanting simple journalist, as is made clear

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, someone no longer wanted
simple means plain
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A writer drops the plain-speaking reporter, and the reason is spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made clear has been clarified or accounted for in words.

clue.text: Attempt to meet holy person for a date

parts.note: an attempt is a try
ST, short for saint, is a holy person

explanation.surface: Trying to meet a saint for a romantic engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret romantic appointment or rendezvous between lovers is the meaning shared.

clue.text: Cricketer all right in second test almost to the end

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other
says the word is taken nearly all the way to its end, losing the final letter

parts.note: test as written, a trial
all right is OK

explanation.surface: A cricketer is fine in the second Test match, nearly lasting to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost to the end' drops the final letter before 'in' places the okay inside. Ben Stokes is England's star all-rounder; a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Stokes is a celebrated England cricketer, an all-rounder and Test captain.

clue.text: Wine trader running short after next to no time

indicators.note: after puts the seller piece behind the moment piece

parts.note: MO, short for moment, is next to no time at all

indicators.note: running short says the word comes up a letter short at its end

parts.note: a trader is a seller

explanation.surface: A wine merchant runs out of stock almost at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a white wine from the valley of the Moselle river in Germany.

clue.text: One may be superior to the musical staff

definitions.text: One may be superior to the musical staff

parts.words: One may be superior to the musical staff
parts.note: a short extra line drawn above the five lines of written music, sitting higher than them, while superior also hints at a snooty member of an orchestra's staff

explanation.surface: A boss who outranks the people working in music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' and 'staff' suggest rank among employees; in music notation they mean placed above the five-line stave.
explanation.definitionFit: Short lines extend the range of notes written above or below the stave in notation.

clue.text: Careful observation — a clue to Keats?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer is a fence post, with out telling you to rearrange it, which gives the poet's name

explanation.surface: A watchful study that offers a hint about the poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the clue: 'out' works as an anagram signal on STAKE, giving KEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Police surveillance of a building or suspect over a long period is this watch.

clue.text: Warm garment that could be glossy

definitions.meaning: an overcoat worn outdoors for warmth
the final layer of paint, which may have a gloss finish

explanation.surface: A cosy coat with a shiny finish.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an outer overcoat; the other is the finishing layer of paint, often gloss.

clue.text: Although mistrustful initially, a saint

parts.note: tho is a short informal spelling of although

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A saint who doubted at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostle who doubted the Resurrection until he saw Christ's wounds became a saint; the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubting apostle was sceptical at first, yet is venerated as a saint.

clue.text: Thrust vigorously? One needs breather in gym

indicators.note: in means the organ goes inside the gym letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is gym class
a lung is a breathing organ, a breather

explanation.surface: A vigorous push needs someone breathing hard in the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge something is to thrust or push it forcefully, as a knife into wood.

clue.text: Strict masters maybe exercising bit of discipline, keeping workers under?

indicators.note: under means the workers piece comes below the rest in this down clue

parts.note: PE, physical education, is exercising

indicators.note: bit of means just the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Stern schoolmasters drilling pupils in a little discipline and keeping their staff down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticklers for detail and rules, such as fussy teachers, fit this description.

clue.text: Weigh up masses, some but not all

indicators.note: says only part of the words masses and some is used, letters running across them

explanation.surface: Evaluating the crowds, some of them at least.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate or appraise something is to weigh it up.

clue.text: Ring king presented to his mistress?

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A king rings his mistress, or gives her a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn, an actress, was Charles II's famous mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the tolling of a bell, especially at a death, so a ring in that sense.

clue.text: Ruler gets them cut short always

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its opening letters, as in the casual spoken form

parts.note: them as written
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A ruler always cuts others down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' clips them to the colloquial 'em.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeer, more often spelt emir, is a Muslim ruler or prince.

clue.text: Military command roared out starts to rouse many soldiers

indicators.note: out means the letters of the word are knocked out of order
the starts of the following three words supply their opening letters

explanation.surface: A sergeant bellows an order to wake a crowd of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ROARED to ORDERA; 'starts to' takes R, M and S from rouse, many, soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill order telling soldiers to bring their rifles down to rest beside the right foot.

clue.text: Exaggerated description of one owing bank money?

definitions.text: description of one owing bank money?
definitions.meaning: having taken more from an account than it held

explanation.surface: An overdone account of someone in debt to the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal made too extreme is overstated; an account in the red has gone below zero.

clue.text: Like some shows being delayed

definitions.meaning: performed on a skating rink, as ice shows are
put on hold, as a plan kept in the freezer

explanation.surface: Some shows are being postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: Skating spectacles take place on a frozen rink; a plan put aside is said to be in cold storage.

clue.text: The suffering of others banished

indicators.note: banished means the letters are sent away from their places and rearranged

explanation.surface: Other people sent into exile and the pain they endure.
explanation.definitionFit: Throes are violent spasms of pain, as in death throes, so intense suffering.

clue.text: Old-style exams? Swig less ale — very little to be drunk!

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger about into a new order

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very; it is a little of the word

explanation.surface: Advice to a drinker: gulp less beer, barely any at all.
explanation.walkthrough: AS levels are English school exams taken at about 17, now largely phased out.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced Subsidiary qualifications were a former tier of English and Welsh school examination.
